You are solving a logic puzzle from the game "Blue Prince".

There are three boxes: BLUE (left), WHITE (middle), BLACK (right). Each box displays one or more statements.

The rules that make the puzzle uniquely solvable:
- EXACTLY ONE of the three boxes contains the gems; the other two are empty.
- AT LEAST ONE box has ALL of its statements TRUE.
- AT LEAST ONE box has ALL of its statements FALSE.
- The remaining box may be all-true, all-false, or a mix.
- A statement's truth value is determined by the actual state of the world (gem location and the truth values of every statement, including self- and cross-references).

Your task: by logical deduction, determine (a) which box contains the gems, and (b) the truth value of EVERY statement.

Here is the puzzle:

BLUE (left) box:
  [B1] THE BOX WITH NO FALSE STATEMENTS HAS THE GEMS

WHITE (middle) box:
  [W1] A BOX NEXT TO THE BLACK BOX CONTAINS THE GEMS AND THE STATEMENT ABOVE THIS ONE IS TRUE

BLACK (right) box:
  [K1] THE WHITE BOX HAS AT LEAST TWO FALSE STATEMENTS

Think step by step. Then, on the VERY LAST line, output your final answer in EXACTLY this one-line format (nothing after it):

FINAL: gem=<BLUE|WHITE|BLACK>; B1=<T/F>; W1=<T/F>; K1=<T/F>

Label EVERY statement id, and ONLY these: B1, W1, K1 (statement counts: BLUE=1, WHITE=1, BLACK=1). One T or F per id.
Example (format only): FINAL: gem=WHITE; B1=T; W1=T; K1=T

K1 is false: the White box has only one statement, so it cannot have at least two false statements. Thus the Black box is all-false.

Since at least one box must be all-true, at least one of B1 or W1 must be true.

- If the gems were in BLACK, W1 would be false because the White box does not contain the gems. Then B1 would have to be true, but Blue would be the only all-true box and would not contain the gems, contradiction.
- If the gems were in WHITE, W1 could be true or false, but both lead to contradictions: if W1 is false, B1 would need to be true while Blue lacks the gems; if W1 is true, B1 cannot consistently describe a unique all-true box containing the gems.
- Therefore the gems must be in BLUE.

With gems in BLUE, W1 is false because the White box does not contain the gems. K1 is false. So B1 must be true, and indeed Blue is the only all-true box and contains the gems.

FINAL: gem=BLUE; B1=T; W1=F; K1=F

- The BLACK box is black, so the second part of W1 is true. Therefore W1 is true.
- WHITE has only statement W1, so WHITE is a true box.
- “A box next to the BLUE box is true” means WHITE is true, so K1 is true.
- Thus BLACK is also a true box.
- There must be at least one all-false box, so BLUE must be the false box.
